name: Chile

facts.religion: Catholic about 45%, evangelical about 15%, no religion about 35%

snapshot: José Antonio Kast, a hard-right former congressman, took office in March 2026 promising to seal the northern border and deport irregular migrants.
culture: Chile stretches 4,300 kilometres from the Atacama, the world's driest desert, to Patagonian glaciers. It produced two Nobel poets, Gabriela Mistral and Pablo Neruda, and the protest songs of Víctor Jara, killed after the 1973 coup. The cueca is the national dance, and Chilean wine is exported worldwide.
society: Chile is the world's top copper producer and a lithium giant, and was long held up as Latin America's economic model. Huge 2019 protests over inequality led to two failed attempts to replace Augusto Pinochet's constitution. Rising crime and migration from Venezuela have dominated recent politics.
situation: From 1973 to 1990, General Augusto Pinochet ruled Chile after a coup, and thousands were killed or disappeared. Since democracy returned, the country has been run by centre-left and centre-right governments that kept Pinochet's legacy at arm's length. In 2026 Chile inaugurated José Antonio Kast, who campaigned for Pinochet as a young man, its most right-wing leader since the return of democracy (AP via WTOP).

Kast took office on 11 March, replacing the leftist Gabriel Boric, and signed half a dozen emergency decrees on border security and deportations before his first speech. Chile's foreign population doubled between 2017 and 2024, mostly Venezuelans fleeing collapse, and Kast linked them to rising crime, though Chile remains one of the region's safest countries, with a homicide rate of 5.4 per 100,000 (Teleamazonas/AFP). Five days in, he stood among excavators at the Peruvian border to launch a "Border Shield" of trenches and barriers across the Atacama Desert, and sent bills to Congress to make illegal entry a crime and cut migrants' social benefits (NPR via WRVO). He has threatened about 336,000 undocumented migrants with expulsion. Investors welcomed his promise of $6 billion in spending cuts over 18 months, though economists doubt it can be done without hitting social benefits. Two of his ministers once defended Pinochet-era generals in court.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single four-year term with no immediate re-election; Congress has a Chamber of Deputies and Senate. Two attempts to replace the Pinochet-era constitution failed in referendums in 2022 and 2023.
holders: President José Antonio Kast (Republican Party), since March 2026.

eat: Empanadas de pino, beef and onion, for Independence Day
Pastel de choclo, corn and meat pie
Completo, a hot dog loaded with avocado
listen: Nueva canción, Víctor Jara and Violeta Parra
argue: Crime and migration, which drove the 2025 election
A new constitution that voters rejected twice

story: Spain conquered most of Chile but never subdued the Mapuche in the south. Independent in 1818, it won nitrate-rich land in the War of the Pacific. Socialist Salvador Allende was elected in 1970 and overthrown in 1973 by General Augusto Pinochet, whose regime killed or disappeared over 3,000 people and remade the economy along free-market lines. Democracy returned in 1990. Mass protests in 2019 led to two failed attempts at a new constitution.
